title: General GNN framework & GraphSAGE
blurb: Message + aggregation, mean / pool / LSTM aggregators

hook.title: How should a committee combine opinions?
hook.text: Each node holds a committee made of its neighbours' messages. How to combine them is a design choice. **Mean**: take the average opinion. **Pool**: have each member amplify their message through a little megaphone (an MLP), then take the loudest per topic (max). **LSTM**: read the messages one after another like a story, but then reading order would matter, so you must shuffle. GraphSAGE adds a twist: first combine the neighbours, *then* combine that with your own prior opinion by **concatenation**.
hook.recall: Remember the committee: a GNN layer = message + aggregation; GraphSAGE aggregates neighbours first (mean / pool / LSTM), then concatenates with its own embedding.

explore.intro: Node $v$ has $h_v=(1,1)$ and a growing set of neighbour vectors. Switch aggregators and add neighbours.
tasks: Add neighbours with *Sum*, then with *Mean*. Which one depends on the neighbour count?
explore.takeaway: General framework: (1) message, (2) aggregation, (3) layer connectivity, (4) graph augmentation, (5) learning objective. GraphSAGE: $h_v^{(l)}=\sigma(W^{(l)}\cdot\text{CONCAT}(h_v^{(l-1)},\text{AGG}(\{h_u^{(l-1)}\})))$.

options: the sum of all nodes in the graph

build.explanation: Slide 34: two-stage aggregation: first aggregate from node neighbours, then further aggregate over the node itself.
